title: Correlated-Electron Theory of Triplet-Triplet Multiexciton States in Polypentacene
authors: Rupali Jindal, Alok Shukla, Sumit Mazumdar
abstract: We present correlated-electron calculations of optical spin-singlet and triplet-triplet multiexciton states in three- and four-unit pentacene oligomers as microscopic models for polypentacene. The calculations use the Pariser-Parr-Pople Hamiltonian, multiple-reference singles and doubles configuration interaction, and a molecular exciton basis that resolves Frenkel, charge-transfer, and triplet-pair (T1T1) configurations in real space. We find that the complete set of 1(T1T1) eigenstates lies in a narrow, nearly degenerate energy window near the lowest optical exciton and that no eigenstate can be identified with a single localized triplet-pair configuration. Instead, each triplet-pair eigenstate is a quantum superposition of configurations containing all accessible intertriplet separations. This electronic structure explains the perceived absence of intramolecular triplet diffusion in pentacene oligomers, polypentacene, and polytetracene solutions, while leaving open the possibility of intermolecular singlet fission in films with appreciable interchain interactions.
summary: The authors theoretically analyze the multiexciton states in polypentacene oligomers using sophisticated correlated-electron calculations. They demonstrate that the triplet-triplet excited states are highly delocalized quantum superpositions rather than localized pairs. This finding explains why experimental measurements suggest no discrete intramolecular triplet diffusion, challenging previous models of exciton behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates the nature of triplet-triplet multiexciton states (1(T1T1)) in acene oligomers to determine if intramolecular triplet separation is physically possible.
main_result: The 1(T1T1) eigenstates are quantum superpositions of configurations spanning all accessible intertriplet separations, explaining the apparent absence of discrete intramolecular triplet diffusion.
method: Correlated-electron calculations using the Pariser-Parr-Pople (PPP) Hamiltonian solved via Multiple-Reference Singles and Doubles Configuration Interaction (MRSDCI).
model_or_system: The model uses three- and four-unit pentacene oligomers as microscopic representations of polypentacene. The calculations employ a molecular exciton basis to resolve different excitation types.
key_observables: Optical spin-singlet and triplet-triplet multiexciton states; Excited State Absorption (ESA) spectra from 1(T1T1) eigenstates; Triplet binding energy.
important_parameters: Onsite Hubbard repulsion U = 6.7 eV; The system size varies from 2 to 4 pentacene units.
main_assumptions: Electron-vibration interactions are neglected, and the MRSDCI method approximates the inclusion of necessary quadruple excitations.
figures_summary: Figures schematically compare localized-pair vs. configuration-mixed descriptions of eigenstates; specific figures illustrate intermonomer Charge Transfer (CT) channels responsible for labeled ESA peaks in 4Pc.
paper_structure: The paper develops by first establishing the theoretical framework using PPP/MRSDCI, then calculating and analyzing the nature of the 1(T1T1) eigenstates, comparing these findings to experimental TA data, and finally concluding on the implications for triplet diffusion and singlet fission.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses excited-state dynamics in organic semiconductors using advanced correlated electron methods, providing insights into charge/exciton localization and transport mechanisms relevant to molecular electronics and quantum energy conversion.
